During the hearing on Friday, Chief Public Prosecutor Shishir Hiray informed the bench that while a closure report was filed in the case, it was subsequently reopened in 2020. Advocate Niranjan Mundargi, appearing for Goswami, said that the State had reopened the investigation on its own volition without judicial authority, driven by political vendetta. He was referring to the earlier Maha Vikas Aghadi government which was in power in the State in 2020 when the case was reopened and he was arrested. Justice Milind Jadhav took note of the submissions and narrowed the primary legal issue to the scope of State power in reopening closed cases. items.title: Commercial Courts Act 2015 applies to commercial suits filed before its enactment: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has held that the restrictions on appeals under the Commercial Courts Act, 2015 apply even to commercial suits filed before the law came into force. [Yes Bank v. Modi Rubber] A three-judge Bench of Justices V Kameswar Rao, Chandrasekharan Sudha and Amit Mahajan ruled that litigants in such suits cannot claim the wider appellate remedies available under the earlier legal regime merely because the proceedings began before October 23, 2015. "We hold that the provisions of the Commercial Courts Act shall be applicable to suits filed prior to its commencement, even if the suits were converted or re-numbered into commercial suits only on a later date," the judgment stated. The ruling came on a reference arising from an appeal filed by Yes Bank against a March 2019 order that allowed Modi Rubber Limited to amend its plaint in a recovery suit. The suit was filed in 2014 for recovery of ₹33.13 crore with interest and damages. It arose from credit facilities extended by Yes Bank in connection with a joint venture between Modi Rubber’s subsidiary and Continental AG. Although the suit preceded the Commercial Courts Act, it was renumbered as a commercial suit only in 2020.

items.title: Lawyers' instinct to question authority not merely a legacy of freedom struggle, relevant even today: CJI Surya Kant
items.summary: Legal profession's instinct to test any exercise of authority against the values of justice, fairness and rule of law is not merely a legacy of India's freedom movement but remains relevant today, Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant said on Saturday. He was delivering the chief guest's address at the Supreme Court Bar Association's Independence Day function on the Supreme Court lawns. "I believe that instinct to examine the exercise of authority in any form or manner against the values of justice, fairness, and rule of law is not just a legacy of the freedom movement. It remains relevant to us even today, and reminds us of the foundational Constitutional rights that we have inherited, which enable us to protect the civil liberties of individuals," the CJI said. He said lawyers are trained to look beyond the mere existence of a rule and ask whether the exercise of power was consistent with the principles meant to justify it. This, he said, was the question that had confronted British colonial rule - if a government claims to rule through law, can that law deny liberty, equality and dignity to the people it governs. items.title: US court upholds confirmation of Devas’ $562.5 million arbitral award against ISRO owned Antrix
items.summary: The United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit has upheld the confirmation of a $562.5 million arbitral award obtained by Devas Multimedia against Antrix Corporation, the commercial arm of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). A Bench of Circuit Judges Eric D Miller and Lucy H Koh and District Judge Donald W Molloy ruled that American courts had jurisdiction to enforce the award against Antrix, a corporation wholly owned by the Indian government. The opinion was authored by Judge Koh. According to law firm Baker Botts, which represented Devas, the award is now worth more than $2 billion with accrued interest. The dispute arose from a 2005 agreement under which Antrix agreed to build, launch and operate two satellites and lease 70 MHz of India’s S-band spectrum to Devas. Antrix terminated the agreement in 2011 after the Indian government decided against providing an S-band orbital slot for commercial activities. Devas then initiated arbitration before the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC). items.title: Nip it in the bud: Bombay High Court calls for aggressive sterilisation of stray dogs
items.summary: The Bombay High Court on Friday suggested that the Maharashtra government aggressively implement the Animal Birth Control (ABC) programme to halt the growth of stray dog population. A division bench of acting Chief Justice Ravindra V Ghuge and Justice Gautam A Ankhad emphasised that prioritising sterilisation of adult dogs over managing expanding numbers would naturally address the issue. Acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad The bench observed that halting the growth of the stray dog population is key to resolving the broader crisis. “Your administration must realise one thing, that if you implement that ABC program aggressively, there will be no growth of dogs (stray). Every dog which is sterilised through the ABC program, there can be no procreation,” ACJ Ghuge said. He emphasised that instead of trying to catch hold of the growing number of dogs, the State could catch adult dogs and sterilise them. “If there is no birth of puppies later, then you are nipping the disease in the bud.
